sentences.text: I have heard the Ld. Counsel for the complainant and perused the entire record with his assistance.

20. At the very outset, it is pertinent to mention that complainant in order to be entitled to the relief under the Domestic Violence Act, 2005 is required to establish firstly that there is a domestic relationship as defined u/s 2(f) of the abovesaid Act between complainant and respondents and thereafter it is also required to be established that she has been a victim of domestic violence as defined u/s 3 of the said Act.

Domestic relationship has been defined under the Act in Section 2(f) as under : 
(f) "domestic relationship" means a relationship between two persons who live or have, at any point of time, lived together in a shared household, when they are related CC NO. 59/1/12 PS:
SUBZI MANDI KRITIKA JAIN VS. ANKIT JAIN 9/15 by consanguinity, marriage, or through a relationship in the nature of marriage, adoption or are family members living together as a joint family.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 21. It be observed that testimonies of CW1 in this regard have remained unrebutted and unchallenged and therefore, deemed to have been accepted by the respondents.
The respondents have not disputed the factum of domestic relationship at any point of time.
The factum of marriage between complainant and respondent no. 1 is proved through documents Ex. CW1/6 & Ex. CW1/7 i.e. marriage photographs and marriage card respectively.
In view thereof, the domestic relationship between the parties stand proved.
22. It is also incumbent upon the complainant to establish that she has been a victim of domestic violence.
CW 1 / complainant has mentioned at para no. 03 to 32 of the affidavit about various incidents and acts of domestic violence committed upon her by the respondents.

The testimony of CW1/complainant as regards the domestic violence have also remained unrebutted and uncontroverted on account of failure to cross examine her by the respondents and hence deemed to have been accepted by them as true and correct.

The counter claims of respondents have not been proved either during cross examination of CW1/complainant or by leading evidence, hence, factum of being victim of domestic violence has been established.
23. By way of present application, the complainant has prayed for protection order u/s 18 of the Act.

Though the testimony of CW1/complainant has remained unrebutted and uncontroverted but it is on record that the complainant has been residing separately from the respondents at her parental house since 07.02.2012.
The complainant has not narrated any recent incident or acts of domestic violence being committed upon her after the separation.
It be observed that no evidence has been led by the complainant to prove the ownership of shared household.
She has also not brought any evidence to show that respondents are having other immovable properties.

So far as, prayer regarding alienation of her istridhan articles is concerned, it be observed that complainant has not able to prove through cogent evidence that her istridhan articles have been retained by the respondents.

The CC NO. 59/1/12 PS: SUBZI MANDI KRITIKA JAIN VS. ANKIT JAIN 10/15 document Ex. CW1/1 and Ex. CW1/12 i.e. lists of dowry articles are not witnessed by the family members of the parties, which casts a serious doubt over its genuineness.

sentences.text: On the contrary, document Ex. CW1/12 reveals endorsement dated 07.08.2012 made by respondent no. 1 to the effect that complainant has already taken all the jewellery items given at the time of marriage.
It also be observed that in the present case, the sources of dowry articles and expenses incurred in the marriage have been disclosed.
Accordingly, no ground is made out to pass protection order in favour of the complainant.
24. So far as residence order under section 19 is concerned, it be observed that the complainant has made request to allow her to live at shared household.

In this respect, the court is of the view that reinstatement of complainant at the shared household shall create more domestic problems between the parties and therefore the court is not inclined to pass an order seeking reinstatement of complainant in the shared household.
The complainant has prayed for making provision for suitable alternate accommodation or to take a rented premises according to her living standard.

In this regard, the court is of the view that "Maintenance/Monetary'' relief shall include food, clothing,
medical expenses, residence etc., hence, there is no need to direct provision of alternate accommodation or to take rented accommodation according to her living standard be made for the complainant.

25. Now coming to Monetary relief under section 20 of the Act, in respect to income and employment of respondent no. 1, complainant has claimed that he is running the business of artificial jewellery and earning about Rs. 1 lac per month.
She has also claimed that respondent no. 1 owns various properties/bank balance and he has no other liability except to maintain her.

In support of the claims she has relied upon documents Ex. CW1/9 i.e. facebook profile of respondent no. 1 containing his personal details including job profile, Ex. CW1/10 i.e. CIBIL consumer credit information report disclosing no liability of loan etc. and Ex. CW1/13 i.e. CC NO. 59/1/12 PS:

SUBZI MANDI KRITIKA JAIN VS. ANKIT JAIN 11/15 certified copy of anticipatory bail application U/s 438 Cr. P.C. of respondent no. 1 containing admission of respondent no. 1 to the effect that he is running business in the area of Bayawer, Rajasthan.

sentences.text: 26. In this regard, though the testimony of CW1/complainant has remained unchallenged and unrebutted but she has not come up with substantial material in order to prove her claims in respect to employment and income of respondent no. 1.
It be observed that complainant has not filed any conclusive document to prove the income of respondent no. 1 of Rs. 1 lac per month from the business of artificial jewellery.
She has also not led any evidence to prove various properties and bank balance of respondent no. 1.

However, the court cannot turn blind eye to the fact that respondent no. 1 has not been truthful in disclosing his true income and has made all possible efforts to conceal his income from all sources.
The court in its order dated 06.02.2014 has already observed that respondent no. 1 has mentioned several contradictory facts in his written statement and income affidavit.

In income affidavit he has mentioned of having own business in the column of past occupation but claimed to have suffered immense loss in the said business but in written statement he has not stated so.
It appears that the same has been done in order to cover up his income reflected in ITRs filed by him.
It is notable that he has also not mentioned the details of said business, which goes on to suggest falsity of his claims.

It is also notable that he has mentioned in document Ex. CW1/13 that he is running business in the area Bayawer, Rajasthan, which proves falsity of his claim of being an employee in an artificial jewellery shop.
The respondent no. 1 has also not mentioned the name of the shop where he is working currently.

28. Now coming to educational qualification of respondent no. 1, in income affidavit he has declared to be 10th class pass but document Ex. CW1/9 shows otherwise, whereas he has claimed himself to be a student of Engineering College and graduated from Gyan Ganga Vidhyapeeth.

It be observed that respondent no. 1 has claimed having liabilities to maintain his parents and sister but in income affidavit, he has mentioned at para no. 5 that his sister is doing a private job and living separately at Mussorie and his mother Smt. Manju Lata is the owner of residential house.
There is nothing on record to prove the source of income of his mother so as to enable her to purchase a residential accommodation.
29. It is notable that as per CIBIL consumer credit information report, the respondent no. 1 is having no loan liabilities.

It is further notable that in income affidavit, the respondent no.1 has denied maintaining bank accounts, vehicles, cellphone and incurring maintenance charges, but his ITR, 201213 reflects otherwise.
It shows expenditures on phone, electricity, petrol etc., and also reflects bank accounts details of the company owned by the respondents.

It is further notable that the respondent no. 1 has denied doing jewellery business on the one hand but on the other hand, his ITRs provide details of trading account, profit & loss account, capital account balance sheet etc.,
which collectively prove that the business of artificial jewellery is being run by him and has share in the said business.
The ITRs also disclose that the respondent no. 1 has got Rs. 20,000/ as salary besides other facilities and around Rs. 65,000/ have been paid as salary to other employees.
It is also reflected that Rs 9000/has been paid towards litigation expenses.
It is also notable that the ITR reflecting loss in business was prepared on 21.09.2013 after the court direction.
The respondent no. 1 has not proved his claim of sufferance of loss in the business by leading evidence.

In view of the forgoing CC NO. 59/1/12 PS: SUBZI MANDI KRITIKA JAIN VS. ANKIT JAIN 13/15 discussions, it is proved that the respondent no. 1 is not truthful in disclosing his actual employment & income and adverse inference is required to be drawn.

opennyai_summary.facts:
The present complaint has been filed by the complainant U/s 12 of Domestic Violence Act, 2005 against her husband and in laws.
SUBZI MANDI KRITIKA JAIN VS. ANKIT JAIN 2/15
opennyai_summary.issue: 20. At the very outset, it is pertinent to mention that complainant in order to be entitled to the relief under the Domestic Violence Act, 2005 is required to establish firstly that there is a domestic relationship as defined u/s 2(f) of the abovesaid Act between complainant and respondents and thereafter it is also required to be established that she has been a victim of domestic violence as defined u/s 3 of the said Act.
opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
Domestic relationship has been defined under the Act in Section 2(f) as under : 
(f) "domestic relationship" means a relationship between two persons who live or have, at any point of time, lived together in a shared household, when they are related CC NO. 59/1/12 PS:
SUBZI MANDI KRITIKA JAIN VS. ANKIT JAIN 9/15 by consanguinity, marriage, or through a relationship in the nature of marriage, adoption or are family members living together as a joint family.
22. It is also incumbent upon the complainant to establish that she has been a victim of domestic violence.
The counter claims of respondents have not been proved either during cross examination of CW1/complainant or by leading evidence, hence, factum of being victim of domestic violence has been established.
23. By way of present application, the complainant has prayed for protection order u/s 18 of the Act.
The complainant has not narrated any recent incident or acts of domestic violence being committed upon her after the separation.
It be observed that no evidence has been led by the complainant to prove the ownership of shared household.
She has also not brought any evidence to show that respondents are having other immovable properties.
So far as, prayer regarding alienation of her istridhan articles is concerned, it be observed that complainant has not able to prove through cogent evidence that her istridhan articles have been retained by the respondents.
It also be observed that in the present case, the sources of dowry articles and expenses incurred in the marriage have been disclosed.
Accordingly, no ground is made out to pass protection order in favour of the complainant.
24. So far as residence order under section 19 is concerned, it be observed that the complainant has made request to allow her to live at shared household.
In this respect, the court is of the view that reinstatement of complainant at the shared household shall create more domestic problems between the parties and therefore the court is not inclined to pass an order seeking reinstatement of complainant in the shared household.
The complainant has prayed for making provision for suitable alternate accommodation or to take a rented premises according to her living standard.
In this regard, the court is of the view that "Maintenance/Monetary'' relief shall include food, clothing,
medical expenses, residence etc., hence, there is no need to direct provision of alternate accommodation or to take rented accommodation according to her living standard be made for the complainant.
25. Now coming to Monetary relief under section 20 of the Act, in respect to income and employment of respondent no. 1, complainant has claimed that he is running the business of artificial jewellery and earning about Rs. 1 lac per month.
SUBZI MANDI KRITIKA JAIN VS. ANKIT JAIN 11/15 certified copy of anticipatory bail application U/s 438 Cr. P.C. of respondent no. 1 containing admission of respondent no. 1 to the effect that he is running business in the area of Bayawer, Rajasthan.
It be observed that complainant has not filed any conclusive document to prove the income of respondent no. 1 of Rs. 1 lac per month from the business of artificial jewellery.
She has also not led any evidence to prove various properties and bank balance of respondent no. 1.
However, the court cannot turn blind eye to the fact that respondent no. 1 has not been truthful in disclosing his true income and has made all possible efforts to conceal his income from all sources.
From the said documents, it is not proved that the miscarriage was caused due to atrocities committed by the respondents.
No other cogent evidence has been brought on record to prove mental & emotional injuries caused to her.
opennyai_summary.decision:
Having regard to the facts and circumstances of the case,
status of the parties and their responsibilities, respondent no.1 is directed to pay Rs. 20,000/ (
Rupees Twenty Thousand) per month as maintenance to the complainant from the date of filing of the present petition.
Payment shall be made by 10th of every month by instant money order or be deposited in the bank account of the complainant.
Arrears shall be cleared within 6 months.
Maintenance awarded in other proceedings shall be liable to adjustment.
In order to prove her claims in this respect, complainant has filed the documents Ex. CW1/2 (collectively), Ex. CW1/3 to Ex. CW1/5 (collectively).
Accordingly, the prayer of compensation is also declined.
Vide separate detailed order, the present complaint   accordingly.
